cases.vignette:
A 3-month-old boy presented with multiple cutaneous red papules first noticed at birth. The papules increased in number and size over months, involving the head and neck, trunk, extremities, right palm, mons pubis, and buttocks, reaching a total of 39 lesions. Some lesions were associated with ulceration and bleeding. The patient was born at full term via spontaneous vaginal delivery without prenatal care. No history of environmental or hazardous substance exposure. Paternal family history was unremarkable; maternal family history was unknown.

cases.vignette:
A 26-year-old man presented with a several-year history of persistent round lesions with a scar-like appearance on his face. His condition had previously been diagnosed and treated unsuccessfully. He denied experiencing previous inflammation and had no history of chicken pox, acne or traumatic lesions in those areas.

Several round atrophic lesions on his face, symmetric and bilateral, located especially on the malar and preauricular areas, with a diameter of 5 to 10 mm. The skin lesions were not indurated and displayed no epidermal changes.

evidence_items.content: Demographics: man in his 70s
Chief complaint: persistent eruption of 5 years' duration
Previous treatments: oral antibiotics, oral doxepin, UV-B phototherapy, oral methotrexate
History of HSV-2 infection on the buttocks
Lesion description: multiple erythematous and violaceous plaques and nodules
Lesion location: superior buttocks and intergluteal cleft bilaterally
Lesion characteristics: smooth and firm
Syphilis screen results: negative
Molecular analysis of T-cell receptor gamma gene: weak clonal band in a polyclonal background
Repeat molecular studies: no evidence of clonal rearrangement
First biopsy findings: dense infiltrate of atypical CD4+ small to medium-sized lymphocytes in the upper dermis
First biopsy findings: admixed with eosinophils and plasma cells, no epidermotropism
Second biopsy findings: similar to prior findings, but with more dense and atypical infiltrate showing epidermotropism
Figure 1 Title: Clinical Presentation
Figure 2 Title: Histopathological Findings

cases.vignette:
A man in his 70s presented with a persistent eruption of 5 years' duration. He had been treated with oral methotrexate for presumed chronic dermatitis after treatments with oral antibiotics, oral doxepin, and UV-B phototherapy had failed. Investigation of medical records revealed a history of HSV-2 infection on the buttocks prior to the development of the current eruption at the same site.

Multiple erythematous and violaceous plaques and nodules clustered on the superior buttocks and intergluteal cleft bilaterally. The lesions were smooth and firm.

- Laboratory tests: Syphilis screen results were negative. Molecular analysis of the T-cell receptor gamma gene showed a weak clonal band in a polyclonal background. Repeat molecular studies showed no evidence of clonal rearrangement.- Pathological findings:  First biopsy: Dense infiltrate of atypical CD4+ small to medium-sized lymphocytes in the upper dermis admixed with eosinophils and plasma cells. Epidermotropism was not identified.  Second biopsy: Similar to prior findings, but with more dense and atypical infiltrate showing epidermotropism.

cases.vignette:
A man in his 40s with a medical history of factor VII deficiency hemophilia presented with acute hypoxic respiratory failure. Following admission, he was intubated with prone positioning, and treatment was initiated. He was also found to have Staphylococcus hemolyticus bacteremia. Three days after admission, the patient developed erythema and edematous necrotic plaques of the bilateral ears. No devices had been used on the ears. The necrosis progressed during the following days, primarily involving the earlobe of the right ear and a large portion of the helix of the left ear.

Erythematous plaque (2 cm) with overlying eschar on the right earlobe. Multiple erythematous edematous erosions with eschar and crust on the helical rim of the left ear.

- Biopsy findings:    Image Title: Hematoxylin-eosin−stained biopsy specimens    Image Description: Detached epidermis with full-thickness necrosis overlying sparse inflammation associated with necrosis of adnexal epithelia, including folliculosebaceous units and eccrine glands. Epidermal and dermal necrosis and ulceration with necrosis of the eccrine glands.

Figure B: Hematoxylin-eosin staining showing dermal-based tumor cells arranged in a vague nodular configuration

cases.vignette:
A 74-year-old man with a history of multiple squamous cell carcinomas that were treated with Mohs micrographic surgery presented with a tender, enlarging scalp lesion of 6 months' duration.

Skin examination revealed a 5-mm bright pink, dome-shaped papule with overlying vessels located at the crown of the scalp. There was no purulent discharge or overlying skin changes.

Chief complaint: 2-year history of progressive eruption of papules and nodules all over his body
Lesions did not cause pain or itching
No family history of cutaneous disorders
Lesions were present on the scalp, face, neck, trunk, and limbs, including the axillae and inguinal regions
Nasal and oropharyngeal mucosa were also affected
Lesions were 2 to 10 mm in diameter
Coalescing, yellow-brown nodules and plaques up to 4 cm in diameter on the face, trunk, and limbs
Routine laboratory test results and serum chemistry with serum lipid levels were within normal ranges
No clinical evidence of internal involvement was found on ultrasonography, computed tomography, or magnetic resonance imaging results
Dense diffuse cellular infiltrate composed mainly of foamy histiocytic cells and multinucleated Touton cells mixed with lymphocytes and eosinophils

Figure 1
Figure 2

cases.vignette:
A 7-year-old boy presented with a 2-year history of progressive eruption of papules and nodules all over his body. The lesions did not cause pain or itching. The patient had no family history of cutaneous disorders.

Multiple yellow to reddish brown firm papules and nodules were present on the scalp, face, neck, trunk, and limbs, including the axillae and inguinal regions. The nasal and oropharyngeal mucosa were also affected. The lesions were 2 to 10 mm in diameter with coalescing, yellow-brown nodules and plaques up to 4 cm in diameter on the face, trunk, and limbs.

Routine laboratory test results and serum chemistry with serum lipid levels were within normal ranges. No clinical evidence of internal involvement was found on ultrasonography, computed tomography, or magnetic resonance imaging results.

Dense diffuse cellular infiltrate composed mainly of foamy histiocytic cells and multinucleated Touton cells mixed with lymphocytes and eosinophils. Spindle cells and increased numbers of collagen fibers in a storiform arrangement were visible in the deep dermis.

Positive for CD68 and CD163, but negative for S100, CD1a, and Langerin.

She had one 2 mm erosion on the soft palate of her mouth; her face was otherwise spared.

- Atypical cells positive for myeloperoxidase, CD15, CD43, CD45, CD68, TIA-1

A 30-year-old woman presented with a 15-year history of recurrent ankle swelling and intermittent painful and tender nodules on her legs and feet. Her symptoms worsened during two pregnancies, which were carried to term. One and a half years before admission, she experienced escalation of symptoms, with nodules progressing to painful leg ulcers, and developed intermittent oral and vaginal ulcerations. Previous treatments included wound care, leg compression, systemic corticosteroids, methotrexate, hydroxychloroquine, aspirin, and rivaroxaban.

Patient had large, extremely tender, irregularly shaped circumferential leg ulcers, with violaceous and purpuric borders, areas of eschar, and a fibrinous base. cases.vignette:

The sore throat persisted despite a trial of omeprazole and fluctuated in intensity over the following months. Several months later, the patient began to experience dysphonia along with odynophagia. Throughout this course, the patient had no systemic symptoms (fever, weight loss, myalgias) or pulmonary symptoms.
